decorators.description: These are the currently configured decorators grouped by stream:
decorators.title: Decorators Configuration

decorators_update.drag_and_drop: Use drag and drop to change the execution order of the decorators.
decorators_update.no_decorators_placeholder: There are no decorators configured for any stream.
decorators_update.read_only: Read only access - you need permission to edit the selected stream
decorators_update.select_stream: Select the stream for which you want to change the set of default decorators.
decorators_update.select_type: Select the type to create a new decorator for this stream:

events.backlog_size_help: Amount of log messages included in a notification by default.
events.catch_up_window_help: If Event processor execution is behind schedule, queries on older data will be run with this window size to speed up processing. (If the "search within the last" setting of an event definition is greater, this setting will be ignored)
events.retry_period_help: Amount of time after which a failed notification is resend. (Minimum is 0 or immediate retry)
events.search_timeout_help: Amount of time after which an Elasticsearch query is interrupted. (Minimum timeout is 1s)
events.tcp_keepalive_help: If enabled, http connections for notifications will send TCP keep-alive probes
events.tcp_keepalive_label: Send TCP keep-alive probes for notification connections
events.title: Events Configuration

markdown.allow_all_sources_help: If enabled, images can be embedded from all sources.
markdown.allowed_sources_help: Allowed image sources for image embedding markdown documents.
markdown.description: These settings can be used to configure Markdown rendering in different parts of the product, including the Text/Markdown widget. When changing settings for allowed image sources, the page will be reloaded afterwards to make sure they are applied.
markdown.title: Markdown Configuration

mcp.description: Activate MCP (Model Context Protocol) to enable LLM-powered communication and automation with your cluster.
mcp.documentation_hint: See the <docsLink>MCP connection documentation</docsLink> for client setup instructions.
mcp.title: MCP Server Configuration

message_processors.description: The following message processors are executed in order. Disabled processors will be skipped.
message_processors.future_timestamp_help: Enable normalisation of timestamps that specify a time significantly ahead of the {{productName}} system time. This typically happens when a log source runs on a server with an incorrect system clock. Future timestamps will be normalised to match the time it was first received by either a {{productName}} Forwarder, or {{productName}}. It is important to prevent future timestamps when making use of the Warm Tier, as this can otherwise degrade performance.
message_processors.global_description: Global Processing Rules are applied after receipt by an Input, and before processing rules applied by Message Processors.
message_processors.grace_period_help: If Future Timestamp Normalisation is enabled, timestamps specifying a time further ahead of the {{productName}} system time than the Grace Period interval will be normalised.
message_processors.order_help: Use drag and drop to change the execution order of the message processors.
message_processors.status_help: Change the checkboxes to change the status of a message processor.
message_processors.title: Message Processors Configuration

password_complexity.description: Configure the minimum password length and character requirements enforced for local users.
password_complexity.min_length_error: Minimum length must be at least 1
password_complexity.min_length_help: Passwords shorter than this length will be rejected.
password_complexity.require_lowercase_help: Password must include at least one lowercase character (a-z).
password_complexity.require_numbers_help: Password must include at least one numeric character (0-9).
password_complexity.require_special_chars_help: Password must include at least one of the following characters:
password_complexity.require_uppercase_help: Password must include at least one uppercase character (A-Z).
password_complexity.title: Password Complexity

permissions.description: These settings can be used to control which entity sharing options are available.
permissions.share_with_everyone_help: Control whether it is possible to share with everyone.
permissions.share_with_users_help: Control whether it is possible to share with single users.
permissions.title: Permissions Configuration

searches.analysis_disabled_fields_help: A ',' separated list of message fields for which analysis features like QuickValues will be disabled in the web UI.
searches.auto_refresh_options_help: Configure the available options for the auto-refresh interval selector as ISO8601 duration
searches.cancellation_timeout_description: The time in seconds per widget after which search execution will be canceled automatically. This minimizes the amount of executed searches and improves performance.
searches.default_auto_refresh_option_help: Select the interval which is used when auto-refresh is started without explicitly selecting one
searches.minimum_refresh_interval_notice: Please note, a minimum refresh interval of <duration /> ({{interval}}) has been configured in the server configuration file. Only intervals which are equal or above the minimum can be used.
searches.query_time_range_limit_description: The maximum time users can query data in the past. This prevents users from accidentally creating queries which span a lot of data and would need a long time and many resources to complete (if at all).
searches.query_time_range_limit_help: The maximum time range for searches. (i.e. "P30D" for 30 days, "PT24H" for 24 hours)
searches.surrounding_filter_fields_help: A ',' separated list of message fields that will be used as filter for the surrounding messages query.
searches.surrounding_options_help: Configure the available options for the surrounding time range selector as ISO8601 duration
searches.title: Search Configuration

sidecar.expiration_threshold_help: Amount of time after which inactive Sidecars are purged from the database.
sidecar.inactive_threshold_help: Amount of time of inactivity after which Sidecars are flagged as inactive.
sidecar.override_sidecar_configuration_help: Override configuration file settings for all Sidecars
sidecar.send_status_updates_help: Send Sidecar status and host metrics from each client
sidecar.title: Sidecars Configuration
sidecar.update_interval_error: invalid (min: 1 second, but less than Inactive threshold)

time_range_presets.add_new: Add new search time range preset
time_range_presets.help: Configure the available search time range presets.

url_allowlist.description: When enabled, outgoing HTTP requests from {{productName}} servers, such as event notifications or HTTP-based data adapter requests, are validated against the allowlists configured here. Because the HTTP requests are made from the {{productName}} servers, they might be able to reach more sensitive systems than an external user would have access to, including AWS EC2 metadata, which can contain keys and other secrets, Elasticsearch and others. Allowlist administrative access is separate from data adapters and event notification configuration.
url_allowlist.title: URL Allowlist Configuration

url_allowlist_form.disable_allowlist_help: Disable the allowlist functionality. Warning: Disabling this option will allow users to enter any URL in {{productName}} entities, which may pose a security risk.
url_allowlist_form.invalid_regex: Not a valid Java regular expression

user.allow_external_tokens: Allow access token for external users
user.allow_external_tokens_help: If enabled, it will allow external users to create access tokens.
user.allow_personal_tokens: Allow users to create personal access tokens
user.allow_personal_tokens_help: If enabled, it will allow users to create access tokens.
user.default_token_ttl_help: Tokens will be automatically invalidated after this amount of time. Example, for 24 hours: PT24H, for 30 days: P30D
user.default_token_ttl_label: Default TTL for new tokens (as ISO8601 Duration)
user.description: These settings can be used to set a global session timeout value.
user.enable_global_session_timeout_help: If enabled, it will be set for all the users.
user.session_timeout_interval_help: Session automatically end after this amount of time, unless they are actively used. Example, for 60 seconds: PT60S, for 60 minutes: PT60M
user.session_timeout_interval_label: Global session timeout interval (as ISO8601 Duration)
user.title: Users Configuration

welcome_page.description: The welcome page can show widgets with message, alert, and event counts, plus a top sources chart. On large or busy clusters, these queries add extra load every time a user opens the welcome page. Disable them below if you want to avoid that load. The widgets will be hidden and their queries will not run.
welcome_page.enable_metrics_help: If disabled, the message, alert, and event count widgets and the top sources chart will be hidden from the welcome page, and their underlying queries will not run. Turn this off on large or busy clusters to reduce query load.
welcome_page.title: Welcome Page
